stories.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian‑occupied Oleshky after humanitarian ceasefire
stories.summary: Russian and Ukrainian authorities said that hundreds of residents were evacuated from the occupied city of Oleshky following a humanitarian ceasefire that the source attributes to U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. Russia’s human‑rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova described the operation as incident‑free and well organised. Ukrainian officials indicated the evacuees would travel through southern Russia and Belarus to reach Ukraine.
stories.why: The evacuation illustrates a rare instance of coordinated humanitarian action between the warring parties.

stories.title: Spain transport minister says he will not resign after high‑speed rail crash
stories.summary: Spain’s transport minister Óscar Puente told a news conference in Madrid that he will not resign following the high‑speed rail collision that has left at least 69 people dead. He said he has “nothing to hide” and reiterated the government’s pledge to investigate the disaster fully. Puente emphasized that his priority is to resolve the problem rather than discuss his position.
stories.why: The statement influences public confidence in how the government is handling a major transportation tragedy.

stories.title: Google launches first data‑center satellite, tests AI model in orbit
stories.summary: Google’s Suncatcher prototype data‑center satellite was launched earlier this month on a SpaceX Falcon 9 ride‑share with more than 100 other spacecraft. The 1 kW satellite carries four TPUs and a pre‑loaded DeepMind Gemma 4 model, which engineers prompted to write a haiku and report orbital conditions after about three weeks of commissioning. Ongoing tests will evaluate TPU performance under space‑borne thermal stress and radiation, which can cause memory bit flips.
stories.why: Demonstrates that high‑power AI inference can operate in orbit, a step toward satellite‑based compute networks.
